title: Spirometry
what: A test of how much air you breathe in and how fast you breathe out. You breathe into the tube of a machine. It is safe and has no needles.
why: For cough, shortness of breath, or wheezing; to find or check asthma and chronic lung disease; before surgery and at health checkups.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes, up to 45 minutes with an inhaler test
tell_doctor: Which inhalers and lung medicines you use. Your doctor will say if you need to skip them before the test
If you recently had a heart attack, or eye, chest, or belly surgery
If you have a cold, a fever, or are coughing up blood now

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Sometimes you are asked not to use your inhaler for a few hours before the test. Do this only if your doctor says so.

prepare.title: Smoking
prepare.text: Do not smoke for at least 1 hour before the test.

prepare.title: Food and activity
prepare.text: Do not eat a big meal for 2 hours before, and no coffee in the morning. Do not rush to the room. Sit for 15 minutes first.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: Wear loose clothes. A tight waistband or belt makes it hard to breathe in deeply.

steps: The nurse measures your height and weight. Normal values depend on them
You sit down and a clip is put on your nose
You seal your lips tightly around a disposable mouthpiece
You breathe calmly, then on command take the deepest breath you can
Then right away you breathe out as hard as you can, long, all the way
This is repeated 3 or 4 times to get the best result
Sometimes you inhale medicine from an inhaler and repeat the test after 15 to 20 minutes
feel: You need to try hard. The test depends on your effort
You may feel dizzy or want to cough. It passes in a minute, and you can rest between tries
after: You can go back to your day right away
The report is usually given right away or the same day
Your doctor will explain the result

faq.q: Why is spirometry repeated several times?
faq.a: The result depends on how hard you breathe out. Several similar tries are needed for accurate data.

faq.q: Why inhale medicine during the test?
faq.a: It is a check to see if breathing gets easier. It helps tell asthma apart from other lung diseases.

reminders.text: Spirometry tomorrow. Bring your inhaler. Skip it only if your doctor told you to.
